what: The score combines generalized radial-savings insertion cost, `delta - distance(depot, customer)`, with a capacity-packing penalty and a capped isolation reward. The packing term measures residual capacity after the best feasible single follow-up customer and becomes stronger as the route fills. Runtime is O(|route| + |unassigned|) per evaluated position with O(1) extra space.
why: Subtracting depot distance prevents ordinary cheapest insertion from systematically favoring depot-near customers; with a one-customer route it naturally favors customers close to the farthest seed. The packing signal helps avoid capacity fragments, especially under heterogeneous demands, while the small isolation reward reduces the chance that spatial outliers are stranded for expensive later routes. The positional insertion delta still chooses a locally coherent slot, leaving crossing cleanup to 2-opt. The coefficients are conservative and scale-free, but the one-step packing statistic cannot detect multi-customer demand combinations, and isolation or radial savings may be less helpful on unusual geometries or weakly capacitated instances.
